questionText:
Consider the following grammar $G$, with $S$ as the start symbol. The grammar $G$ has three incomplete productions denoted by (1), (2), and (3).

$$S \rightarrow daT \mid \underline{\quad (1) \quad}$$
$$T \rightarrow aS \mid bT \mid \underline{\quad (2) \quad}$$
$$R \rightarrow \underline{\quad (3) \quad} \mid \epsilon$$

The set of terminals is $\{a, b, c, d, f\}$. The FIRST and FOLLOW sets of the different non-terminals are as follows.

$$\text{FIRST}(S) = \{c, d, f\}, \; \text{FIRST}(T) = \{a, b, \epsilon\}, \; \text{FIRST}(R) = \{c, \epsilon\}$$
$$\text{FOLLOW}(S) = \text{FOLLOW}(T) = \{c, f, \$\}, \; \text{FOLLOW}(R) = \{f\}$$

Which one of the following options CORRECTLY fills in the incomplete productions?
explanation:
Step 1: Determine Production (1) for $S$
We know that $\text{FIRST}(S) = \{c, d, f\}$.
The given production $S \rightarrow daT$ contributes $d$ to $\text{FIRST}(S)$.
To account for $c$ and $f$ in $\text{FIRST}(S)$:
If $(1)$ is $S \rightarrow Rf$, then $\text{FIRST}(Rf) = \text{FIRST}(R) \setminus \{\epsilon\} \cup \{f\}$ (since $\epsilon \in \text{FIRST}(R)$).
Since $\text{FIRST}(R) = \{c, \epsilon\}$, we get $\text{FIRST}(Rf) = \{c\} \cup \{f\} = \{c, f\}$.
This correctly gives $\text{FIRST}(S) = \{c, d, f\}$.
Hence, production (1) must be $S \rightarrow Rf$.

Step 2: Determine Production (2) for $T$
We are given $\text{FIRST}(T) = \{a, b, \epsilon\}$.
The productions $T \rightarrow aS \mid bT$ contribute $a$ and $b$ to $\text{FIRST}(T)$.
To get $\epsilon \in \text{FIRST}(T)$, production (2) must be $T \rightarrow \epsilon$.

Step 3: Determine Production (3) for $R$
We are given $\text{FIRST}(R) = \{c, \epsilon\}$.
To derive $c$, the RHS of $R$ must start with $c$.
In option (A), (3) is $R \rightarrow cTR$, which gives $\text{FIRST}(cTR) = \{c\}$.

Thus, Option (A) correctly satisfies all given FIRST and FOLLOW constraints.
